req-pm-bit-cursor-1.text: A Physical Parser MUST move the bit cursor by these rules:

req-pm-bit-cursor-2.text: Consecutive bddo:bitLength fields pack contiguously: each consumes the next bitLength bits from the current bit offset, advancing the cursor (rolling into the next byte when it reaches 8).

req-pm-bit-cursor-3.text: Bits are consumed within each byte per the effective bddo:bitOrder: bddo:MSBFirst takes bits from the most-significant end first; bddo:LSBFirst from the least-significant end.

req-pm-bit-cursor-4.text: Every bit keeps its significance: under bddo:MSBFirst the first bit taken is the most significant bit of the field's value, under bddo:LSBFirst the least significant (as DEFLATE and GIF read their codes), so a 3-bit field read LSBFirst from 0xB4 is 4, the low three bits' value. A field spanning a byte boundary continues into the next byte in the same bit order, its later bits more significant under LSBFirst and less significant under MSBFirst.

req-pm-bit-cursor-5.text: The bit cursor realigns to the next whole byte boundary before any byte-oriented read (a field without bitLength), before bddo:alignment, and at the end of a Struct; partial bits before the boundary are skipped.

req-pm-bit-cursor-6.text: A bit read that would cross the end of the innermost bounded region (or |S|) raises a bounds error.

req-pm-byte-order-1.text: A Physical Parser MUST read a multi-byte integer or float in the byte order given by the first of the following that applies:

req-pm-byte-order-2.text: The data type's own byte order: an explicit big- or little-endian type such as bddo:uint32be or bddo:float64le always reads in its own order.

req-pm-byte-order-3.text: The field's own declaration: bddo:endianness on the field, or the first rule of the field's bddo:hasConditionalEndianness whose condition holds, evaluated just before the field is read.

req-pm-byte-order-4.text: The containing struct's own declaration: its bddo:endianness, or its resolved bddo:hasConditionalEndianness (below). The two are mutually exclusive.

req-pm-byte-order-5.text: The byte order inherited from the enclosing struct: the order that was in force (by this same list) for the field through which this struct is being parsed. This applies equally to a struct re-parsed from a decoded sub-stream.

req-pm-byte-order-7.text: A processor MUST resolve a struct's conditional byte order as follows.

req-pm-conformance-1.text: It MUST implement every rule of this document that the classes it claims require, and it MUST NOT silently mis-parse a description that uses a construct outside them (see ).

req-pm-conformance-classes-1.text: abnd:nestedProfile is optional in this version: a Bundle Processor that does not assemble nested profiles MUST reject a bundle profile that uses one with Unsupported feature.

req-pm-conformance-classes-2.text: Its output MUST be a description that a Physical Parser (and, when the source declares mappings, a Semantic Emitter) processes exactly as it would the equivalent hand-written RDF.

req-pm-conformance-classes-3.text: A refusal SHOULD be raised when the description is loaded rather than when the construct is first met in a stream, and MUST be raised no later than the first time the construct would affect the result.

req-pm-conformance-classes-4.text: A processor MUST NOT ignore a construct and parse on as though it were absent: a partly understood description yields a plausible but wrong tree, which is worse than no tree.

req-pm-conformance-classes-5.text: A processor MUST state which classes and which optional features it claims.

req-pm-conformance-classes-6.text: Tree documents and grouped key/value headers are no class's requirement: a processor that claims them MUST implement them exactly as specifies, and one that does not MUST reject a description that uses them, when the description is loaded, and MUST NOT read such a container's fields by byte offset or as a flat header.

req-pm-conformance-classes-7.text: A Physical Parser MUST accept a description that declares a chunked layout and parse the field's bytes.

req-pm-conformance-classes-8.text: A processor that does not claim chunked-layout cell access MUST raise Unsupported feature when a cell is addressed through the chunk table and MUST NOT address the bytes as contiguous cells; one that does not claim other chunk orders MUST reject a dlv:chunkOrder other than dlv:rowMajor or dlv:columnMajor when the description is loaded.

req-pm-conformance-evaluation-1.text: A constraint whose conf:scope is a bddo:Struct MUST be evaluated once for every parsed instance of that struct, after the instance is complete, with instance and self bound to the instance, parent to the struct that holds it and root to the root of the input.

req-pm-conformance-evaluation-2.text: A constraint whose scope is a bddo:Field MUST be evaluated once for every parsed value of that field — each element of a repeated field is one value, and an absent optional field fires nothing — with instance bound to the containing struct and self to the value.

req-pm-conformance-evaluation-3.text: The input's format version is supplied by the caller; an evaluator MUST NOT guess it from the data.

req-pm-conformance-evaluation-4.text: When no version is supplied, every requirement is evaluated and the report MUST state that version scoping was not applied.

req-pm-conformance-evaluation-5.text: An evaluator MUST enforce resource limits on a run (at least the parse limits, and a limit on the number of findings).

req-pm-conformance-evaluation-6.text: When one is reached it MUST either fail with a ResourceLimit error or stop and return a report marked truncated, stating the limit; it MUST NOT return an unmarked partial report.

req-pm-context-1.text: Fields already parsed within the current and ancestor nodes are visible; forward references (to fields not yet parsed) MUST raise an error, except where this document defers an evaluation until its references are bound (, ).

req-pm-context-2.text: The alias is deprecated in HEL 1.0: a processor SHOULD warn when it loads a description that uses it, new descriptions MUST NOT use it, and an HDL compiler never emits it.

req-pm-data-layouts-1.text: Before any cell is addressed, a processor MUST resolve the layout against the field's containing struct: each dlv:dimensionSizeFromField, dlv:dimensionStrideFromField and dlv:cellBitWidthFromField reads the named field (looked up as for bddo:sizeFromField), each dlv:dimensionStrideFromExpression is evaluated, and the first holding arm of dlv:hasConditionalCellDataType and of dlv:hasConditionalDimensionOrder is selected (DLV conditional layout).

req-pm-delimited-records-1.text: A Physical Parser MUST split a delimited container into records and values by these rules:

req-pm-delimited-records-2.text: The bytes are decoded in the bddo:encoding declared on the field through which the container is parsed, or as UTF-8 when none is declared. A malformed sequence is a validation error (recorded as a finding and skipped in a lenient mode); it is never replaced silently. A leading UTF-8 byte order mark is ignored.

req-pm-delimited-records-3.text: The text is split into records at each occurrence of bddo:recordDelimiter (default 0A, LF) that is not inside a quoted value (below). When the delimiter is 0A, a CR immediately before it is removed, so CRLF text reads the same as LF text. A record delimiter at the very end yields no final empty record.

req-pm-delimited-records-4.text: The first bddo:skipRecords records (default 0) are discarded; then every record that, after leading whitespace, begins with bddo:commentPrefix is discarded.

req-pm-delimited-records-5.text: Values within a record. With bddo:fieldDelimiter, a record is split into values at each occurrence of the delimiter sequence outside a quoted value. With bddo:whitespaceSeparated true, values are separated by runs of space, tab, CR or LF: a run of any length separates exactly two values, and leading and trailing whitespace on the record is ignored; if bddo:recordDelimiter is also absent, the whole content is one flat sequence of values, whose shape comes from the field's layout or repeat count. With neither, a record is a single value.

req-pm-delimited-records-6.text: Quoting. With bddo:quoteChar q, a value that begins with q is quoted: it extends to the next q not immediately followed by another q, may contain the field delimiter, the record delimiter and line breaks, and has its quotes removed; a doubled qq inside it denotes one literal q. With bddo:escapeChar e, e followed by any character yields that character with no delimiter or quote meaning. A quoted value still open at the end of the container is a validation error.

req-pm-delimited-records-7.text: With bddo:trimWhitespace true, leading and trailing whitespace is removed from every key and value.

req-pm-delimited-tables-1.text: A bddo:whitespaceSeparated container with no bddo:recordDelimiter is one sequence of values; every Physical Parser MUST support it.

req-pm-delimited-tables-2.text: A processor MUST bind the records of a table as this paragraph states.

req-pm-emission-1.text: For a Field with hexplain:isEncodedWith A, a processor MUST decode the block with algorithm A (a concept from whichever codec or compression register the profile binds; see for the codecs every processor supports and the Unsupported feature error for the rest); when the field's effective data type is a bddo:Struct, it MUST then re-parse the decoded bytes as a fresh bounded sub-stream against that Struct.

req-pm-emission-2.text: If an enumeration matched, a processor SHOULD also emit the symbolic value (the bddo:enumSymbol IRI, if any) alongside the raw literal.

req-pm-emission-3.text: A Semantic Emitter MUST emit these triples:

req-pm-emission-4.text: For a Struct instance s whose description has hexplain:mapsToClass C, emit <IRI(s)> rdf:type C.

req-pm-emission-5.text: For a Field with hexplain:mapsToProperty P, emit <IRI(parent)> P "value"^^xsdType. If the field also carries hexplain:valueExpression E, emit instead the value obtained by evaluating E in the field's context (e.g. fixed-point or unit scaling), typed with hexplain:valueDatatype if given, else the natural datatype of the HEL result.

req-pm-emission-6.text: For a Field with hexplain:mapsToObjectProperty P, emit <IRI(parent)> P o, where o is the IRI minted for the struct instance the field holds when its data type is a bddo:Struct, or the bddo:enumSymbol IRI of the matched bddo:EnumValue when the field carries an enumeration; a value that has neither emits nothing.

req-pm-emission-7.text: For a Field with hexplain:hasConditionalMapping, evaluate rules in order and emit the property of the first rule whose condition holds.

req-pm-emission-8.text: A repeated field emits one such triple per element, in element order; a Null element, like an unbound field, emits nothing.

req-pm-emission-9.text: For a Field with hexplain:hasDataLayout, the layout (DLV) governs how the multi-dimensional cells are addressed; a processor MAY additionally emit per-cell triples but is not required to materialize them.

req-pm-errors-1.text: Processors MUST distinguish and report the following conditions rather than emit a silently-wrong graph:

req-pm-errors-3.text: Bounds error | A read would pass the end of the stream or the innermost bounded region (or a negative offset).

req-pm-errors-4.text: Validation error | bddo:hasFixedValue mismatch; for a multi-part asset, a required part with no file, a part count outside abnd:minParts..abnd:maxParts, or a file matching no part spec or several ().

req-pm-errors-5.text: Checksum error | bddo:Checksum mismatch; an integrity-check mismatch inside a codec (zlib Adler-32, gzip CRC-32, length or header CRC).

req-pm-errors-6.text: Type / HEL error | A HEL type error, division/modulo by zero, undefined name, forward reference, or an array subscript out of range; asset.X read before part X is parsed or naming a part the asset does not have, and the asset root or partExtension() in a part parsed on its own (); a malformed HEL expression (one the HEL grammar does not generate, including an out-of-range literal, an unknown escape or a call with the wrong number of arguments), which SHOULD be raised when the description is loaded and is this category, not a Description error, even then.

req-pm-errors-7.text: Dispatch error | No bddo:DataTypeRule matched and no default bddo:dataType exists.

req-pm-errors-8.text: Description error | The description itself is inconsistent: two dispatch arms with one key, both dispatch mechanisms on one field, an empty terminator, a variable-length field with no extent, an unbound namespace prefix, cyclic cross-part references, two part specs described by structs sharing a local name, a malformed fixed value, a packed width on a non-integer cell type, a bddo:repeatUntil on a text container, a codec parameter that is unknown, missing or out of range. SHOULD be raised when the description is loaded.

req-pm-errors-9.text: SHOULD be raised when the description is loaded.

req-pm-errors-10.text: Unsupported feature | The description uses a construct outside the conformance classes the processor claims, or an optional feature it does not claim (for example a codec beyond the minimum set, or a chunk order other than row- or column-major). The asset root and partExtension() outside an asset are a Type / HEL error, not this (). Only those; see Refusal. SHOULD be raised when the description is loaded, and MUST be raised no later than the first time the construct would affect the result. Distinct from a Description error: the description is valid, this processor cannot run it.

req-pm-errors-11.text: SHOULD be raised when the description is loaded, and MUST be raised no later than the first time the construct would affect the result.

req-pm-errors-12.text: ResourceLimit | A configured resource limit (input bytes, nesting depth, visited nodes, materialized or decoded bytes, HEL nesting, emitted triples) or an implementation wall-clock limit or cancellation was exceeded. Fatal in every mode; never a partial result.

req-pm-errors-13.text: A processor MAY offer a lenient mode that records errors as annotations in G and continues; the default mode SHOULD halt on the first error.

req-pm-errors-14.text: A lenient mode MUST NOT continue past a ResourceLimit, Description or Unsupported feature error.

req-pm-errors-15.text: A HEL type error, division/modulo by zero, undefined name, forward reference, or an array subscript out of range; asset.X read before part X is parsed or naming a part the asset does not have, and the asset root or partExtension() in a part parsed on its own (); a malformed HEL expression (one the HEL grammar does not generate, including an out-of-range literal, an unknown escape or a call with the wrong number of arguments), which SHOULD be raised when the description is loaded and is this category, not a Description error, even then.

req-pm-introduction-1.text: Everything here is REQUIRED behaviour for a conforming processor unless marked otherwise.

req-pm-iri-minting-1.text: To make the instance graph queryable, every emitted subject MUST have a stable, deterministic IRI.

req-pm-iri-minting-2.text: If B is absent, a processor MUST choose a base itself (for example a fresh urn:uuid: IRI) and report it with the graph.

req-pm-iri-minting-3.text: A processor MAY offer alternative minting policies (e.g. hash-based or field-derived keys) but MUST document them and MUST be deterministic: parsing the same bytes with the same description and base IRI MUST yield an isomorphic graph.

req-pm-key-value-1.text: A processor MUST locate the fields of a key/value header as this paragraph states.

req-pm-minimum-codecs-1.text: A processor MUST decode every registered codec it claims to support, MUST state which ones those are, and MUST raise Unsupported feature for any other.

req-pm-minimum-codecs-2.text: Every Physical Parser MUST support at least these concepts of the media-encoding register:

req-pm-minimum-codecs-3.text: menc:Store | Identity: the decoded bytes are the stored bytes.

req-pm-minimum-codecs-5.text: menc:Zlib | zlib framing [[RFC1950]] around DEFLATE, including its header and Adler-32 check; an Adler-32 mismatch is a Checksum error.

req-pm-minimum-codecs-6.text: menc:Gzip | gzip framing [[RFC1952]]. A block MAY hold several gzip members; they are decoded in order and their outputs concatenated. A member's CRC-32 or length (ISIZE) mismatch, or a header CRC-16 mismatch, is a Checksum error. Bytes after the last member that do not begin another member are a Validation error.

req-pm-minimum-codecs-7.text: menc:Delta | Delta / horizontal predictor, with the parameters below: each sample is restored by adding the restored sample that precedes it in the same channel.

req-pm-minimum-codecs-9.text: Other values (for example TIFF's floating-point predictor 3) are not defined by this version: a processor MUST refuse them with Unsupported feature.

req-pm-minimum-codecs-10.text: A processor MUST report compressed data that cannot be decoded (truncated, malformed, needing a preset dictionary, or followed by trailing bytes inside a zlib or raw DEFLATE block) as a Validation error.

req-pm-multi-part-assets-1.text: The part count of each spec is the number of files matched to it; it MUST lie within abnd:minParts (default 1 when abnd:required is true, else 0) and abnd:maxParts (default 1 for a spec located by abnd:extension, which names one member; unbounded for a pattern).

req-pm-multi-part-assets-2.text: A part whose description (the struct and every struct reachable from it) reads asset.X.… MUST be parsed after part X; a processor MUST order the parts so that every such reference is to a part already parsed.

req-pm-multi-part-assets-3.text: A processor that is not a Bundle Processor MUST treat the asset root and partExtension() as HEL errors when a single part is parsed on its own, so that a description depending on a sibling part fails rather than reading Null.

req-pm-multi-part-assets-4.text: A part that is carried but not parsed (its spec has no abnd:describedBy) MUST still be minted the same way: its root is <part>#root, which the lifting below links and types, and which carries no triple of its own content.

req-pm-parsefield-1.text: A processor MUST collect arms from the whole description graph, including imported ontologies; two arms with one key are a description error.

req-pm-parsefield-2.text: Only an xsd:hexBinary literal denotes bytes: on a bytes or string field a processor MUST compare it with the field's raw bytes, byte for byte, and on a numeric field it is the field's encoding in the field's byte order and MUST be exactly the field's width.

req-pm-parsefield-3.text: A Physical Parser MUST parse a field by these steps, in this order; a step whose property the field does not declare does nothing:

req-pm-parsefield-4.text: Presence. If bddo:isPresentIf is present and its HEL expression evaluates to false, skip the field (bind it to Null in the context) and return.

req-pm-parsefield-5.text: Derived value. If bddo:valueFromExpression E is present, evaluate E in the field's context (), bind the result under the field's key, and return. The field consumes no bytes and has no byte extent; none of the steps below apply to it. A Null result leaves the field unbound, exactly as an absent optional field.

req-pm-parsefield-6.text: Alignment. If bddo:alignment = a, advance the cursor to the next multiple of a, measured from the start of the current stream: the input stream, or, inside a field decoded by hexplain:isEncodedWith and re-parsed as a struct, the decoded sub-stream, whose offsets start at 0 (Stream metadata). Bounded regions do not move the origin: a field aligned to 4 inside a region starting at offset 6 starts at offset 8, not 10. The same origin applies to an offset-addressed field's aligned target.

req-pm-parsefield-7.text: Addressing. If an offset property is present, compute the target offset from bddo:atOffset / atOffsetFromField / atOffsetFromExpression, relative to bddo:offsetBase: streamStart (the default) counts from the start of the current stream, streamEnd counts backward from |S|, the length of the current stream, and currentPosition from the cursor. The current stream is the input stream or, inside a field decoded by hexplain:isEncodedWith and re-parsed as a struct, the decoded sub-stream (Stream metadata); a bounded region is not a stream, so streamEnd inside one still counts from the end of the stream that holds it. Save the current cursor — the byte position and any partially consumed byte of the bit cursor — seek to the target, parse, then restore the saved cursor, bit position included (an offset field does not advance sibling parsing and does not disturb a run of bit fields) unless offsetBase is currentPosition. A target outside the innermost bounded region raises a bounds error, unless the field declares bddo:seekScope bddo:streamScope: then the target is resolved against the whole stream [0, |S|) and the region bound is suspended for the duration of this one read (and restored before the cursor is).

req-pm-parsefield-8.text: Repetition. If a repetition property is present, determine the iteration policy: a fixed bddo:repeatCount, a count via repeatCountFromField/repeatCountFromExpression, or repeat-until (bddo:repeatUntil, evaluated after each element with the bindings of ). A bddo:repeatUntil on a field whose data type is a text container () is a description error: the container consumes its whole region, so no element could follow the first. Produce an ordered array node; each element is parsed by the single-value procedure below, and the fixed-value, enumeration and bddo:validIf steps apply to each element, self being the element.

req-pm-parsefield-9.text: If bddo:hasDispatchTable is present, a processor MUST evaluate the table's key — the parsed value of bddo:dispatchOnField, or bddo:dispatchOnExpression evaluated exactly as a bddo:DataTypeRule condition is — and select the bddo:DispatchArm of that table whose bddo:armKey equals it (strings by code points, integers numerically); if none matches, it uses bddo:dispatchDefault, else bddo:dataType.

req-pm-parsefield-10.text: Otherwise, if bddo:hasConditionalDataType is present, a processor MUST evaluate each bddo:DataTypeRule in list order and take the effective type from the first whose bddo:condition is true, via its bddo:ruleDataType.

req-pm-parsefield-11.text: Value. If the effective type is a bddo:Struct, recurse via ParseStruct. If it is a bddo:DataType:

req-pm-parsefield-12.text: Every other string literal (an xsd:string, a plain or a language-tagged literal) denotes characters, never hexadecimal digits: on a bytes field a processor MUST compare the field's bytes with the literal's UTF-8 encoding, so "CAFE" matches the four bytes 43 41 46 45 and not CA FE, and on a string field it MUST compare the decoded value with the literal by code points, whatever the field's bddo:encoding (a bddo:utf16le field holding 41 00 42 00 matches "AB").

req-pm-parsefield-13.text: A numeric literal on a numeric field MUST be compared by value at the field's width: an integer field matches an integer literal of equal value however the literal is typed and the field stored ("9994"^^xsd:int matches the integer 9994), and a float field matches the literal's value rounded to the field's format, so "0.1"^^xsd:double on a bddo:float32 field matches the float32 nearest to 0.1.

req-pm-parsefield-14.text: A processor MUST raise a description error, when the description is loaded, for an xsd:hexBinary of another width on a numeric field, a string or Boolean literal on a numeric field, a numeric or Boolean literal on a string or bytes field, a fraction on an integer field, an integer outside the field's range, and a finite value that overflows a float field's format.

req-pm-parsefield-15.text: Enumeration. If bddo:enumeration is present, look up the raw value among the enumeration's bddo:EnumValue resources; the matching symbol/label is attached to the value node (and emitted per ). If the enumeration has bddo:enumIsFlags true, the raw value is a bitmask: every bddo:EnumValue whose raw value's bits are all set in the parsed value matches, and all matching symbols are attached/emitted.

req-pm-parsefield-16.text: Checksum. If bddo:checksum is present, compute the algorithm over the covered byte range — from the first byte of coversFromField, or the offset coversFromExpression yields, to the last byte of coversToField (inclusive), or up to and excluding the offset coversToExpression yields (the two bounds may mix a field and an expression); or the [start, end) range yielded by the deprecated coversExpression — and compare with the stored value; a mismatch raises a checksum error. A coverage bound outside the current (sub-)stream raises a bounds error; a range whose end precedes its start covers nothing and is not checked. The bddo:checksumAlgorithm values are bddo:crc32 (CRC-32 as in zlib), bddo:adler32, bddo:crc16 (CRC-16/CCITT-FALSE: polynomial 0x1021, initial value 0xFFFF), bddo:md5, bddo:sha1 and bddo:sha256; an integer checksum is compared numerically, a digest byte for byte.

req-pm-parsefield-17.text: Constraint. If bddo:validIf E is present, evaluate E once the field is bound (after the fixed-value and checksum checks), with self bound to the field's value (). false raises a validation error; an evaluation failure raises a Type / HEL error, not a validation error, because it reports a defect of the description rather than of the data.

req-pm-parsefield-18.text: Root key. If bddo:rootKeyFromField is present, let k be the parsed value of the named sibling field; if k is a string and the root context has no binding for k, bind this field's value in the root context under k (first occurrence wins). This is what lets a later field say root.k.… about a record inside a repeated sequence.

req-pm-parsefield-19.text: Bind the field's value into node under the field's simple key, and return.

req-pm-parsefield-20.text: A processor MUST raise a description error, when the description is loaded, for each of these:

req-pm-parsefield-21.text: A repeat count and a repeat-until condition on one field: any of bddo:repeatCount, bddo:repeatCountFromField and bddo:repeatCountFromExpression together with bddo:repeatUntil, or two of the three count forms.

req-pm-parsefield-22.text: Two offset forms on one field: two of bddo:atOffset, bddo:atOffsetFromField and bddo:atOffsetFromExpression.

req-pm-parsefield-23.text: A dispatch table and conditional type rules on one field: bddo:hasDispatchTable together with bddo:hasConditionalDataType.

req-pm-parsefield-24.text: More than one value of a functional property on one resource: a property the family's vocabularies or shapes allow at most once (for example two bddo:dataType, two bddo:size, two bddo:endianness or two bddo:hasFixedValue values on one field).

req-pm-parsestruct-1.text: Members MUST be processed in list order.

req-pm-parsestruct-2.text: A Physical Parser MUST parse a struct by these steps, in this order:

req-pm-parsestruct-3.text: If struct has bddo:syncOnMarker, advance the cursor past the next occurrence of the marker bytes: the marker is consumed, and the struct (its start offset and its first field) begins after it. If no occurrence exists, raise a sync error.

req-pm-parsestruct-4.text: Create a new context node n with a back-link to parent; record its start offset.

req-pm-parsestruct-5.text: Bounded region. If struct declares a size (bddo:size / bddo:sizeFromField / bddo:sizeFromExpression), it establishes a bounded region [start, start+size). A read by this struct or any descendant that would cross the region end raises a bounds error, and a descendant's bddo:sizeToEndOfStream resolves to the region end (not |S|). This is what lets length-delimited containers (ISOBMFF/MP4 boxes, EBML, chunk payloads) bound their children. A literal bddo:size establishes the region before the first field is read; a bddo:sizeFromField or bddo:sizeFromExpression establishes it as soon as every field it references is bound (). A region whose end would lie beyond the enclosing region, or a negative size, raises a bounds error.

req-pm-parsestruct-6.text: Resolve the effective byte order and bit order (). The byte order declared by an ancestor struct is inherited, which is what "nearest declaration wins" means: DataType > Field > this Struct (fixed or conditional) > inherited from the enclosing struct > big-endian.

req-pm-parsestruct-7.text: If struct is a bddo:DelimitedRecords (or subclass) or a bddo:TreeDocument, parse it by the container rules of instead of the next step, then continue at the last step.

req-pm-parsestruct-8.text: If struct declared a size, advance the cursor to start+size (skipping any trailing padding/unknown bytes); otherwise the end offset is the current cursor. Record the node's end offset (sizeof = end − start) and return n.

req-pm-recovery-1.text: When reading a field fails, a processor in a lenient mode MUST record the error once and recover by the first of these rules that applies:

req-pm-recovery-2.text: Pointer. A field read at an offset (bddo:atOffset, bddo:atOffsetFromField, bddo:atOffsetFromExpression) that fails leaves the field unbound and does not move the cursor: the saved cursor is restored, as after any offset-addressed read, and parsing continues with the next field.

req-pm-recovery-3.text: Counted sequence of fixed-width elements. A repeated field whose count is known (its repeat count resolved) and whose elements have a fixed width (a data type with a bddo:bitWidth and no bddo:bitLength) is left unbound, and the cursor moves to the field's start plus count × width, or to the end of the innermost bounded region if that comes first; parsing continues with the next field.

req-pm-recovery-4.text: Otherwise, abandon the rest of the struct. The field that failed and every later field of its struct are left unbound, the fields read before it keep their values, and the cursor moves to the struct's declared end (the end of its bounded region, ) or, when it has none, to the end of the innermost enclosing bounded region, or of the current stream. The struct's node, with the fields it has, is bound in its parent, which continues with its next field. Abandoning the root struct ends the parse.

req-pm-recovery-5.text: A processor MUST NOT recover from a ResourceLimit, Description or Unsupported feature error (), and MUST NOT use a recovery rule to skip a read it could have made.

req-pm-resource-limits-1.text: A processor MUST enforce limits on the work of one invocation, and MUST let its user configure each limit below.

req-pm-resource-limits-2.text: Its default configuration MUST allow at least the values below; it MAY allow more, and MUST allow a user to configure lower limits.

req-pm-resource-limits-3.text: When one fires, the result MUST be a ResourceLimit error, never a different or partial parse.

req-pm-resource-limits-4.text: A processor MUST NOT fall back to a cheaper interpretation of the description to finish in time.

req-pm-size-resolution-1.text: A description SHOULD declare at most one.

req-pm-size-resolution-2.text: Its value, or the value of bddo:sizeFromExpression, MUST be an integer; a number written as text is accepted by its numeric value.

req-pm-size-resolution-3.text: A repeat count MUST be a non-negative integer; a negative count is a bounds error, as a negative size is.

req-pm-size-resolution-4.text: A Physical Parser MUST take the first of these cases that matches, and MUST NOT consult the later ones:

req-pm-size-resolution-5.text: Bits. A field with bddo:bitLength occupies that many bits (, bit cursor).

req-pm-size-resolution-6.text: Separated. A field with bddo:separatedBy is read as a separated token (). The bddo:FieldShape forbids combining it with any size or terminator.

req-pm-size-resolution-7.text: Fixed width. A field whose effective data type has a bddo:bitWidth occupies bitWidth / 8 bytes. Size properties on such a field do not change its width and are ignored.

req-pm-size-resolution-8.text: Self-delimiting. A variable-length integer (bddo:varuint, bddo:varint, bddo:sqliteVarint) occupies as many bytes as its encoding says ().

req-pm-size-resolution-9.text: Declared region and terminator. Otherwise (bytes, string, numbers written as text, and fields whose type is a Struct), the field's declared region is given by the first of these that the field declares: bddo:sizeToEndOfStream (up to the end of the innermost bounded region, or of the current stream if there is none), bddo:size, bddo:sizeFromField, bddo:sizeFromExpression. The region starts at the cursor.

req-pm-size-resolution-10.text: A processor MUST read a repeated field's extent as follows.

req-pm-struct-size-1.text: The size MUST NOT reference a field of this struct that has not been bound when the struct's field list is exhausted (a field declared later than every field that could supply it, or one skipped by bddo:isPresentIf): that is a forward reference and raises a Type / HEL error.

req-pm-struct-size-2.text: The struct MUST NOT be left unbounded instead.

req-pm-struct-size-3.text: A processor MUST apply a struct-level size as this section states.

req-pm-terminators-1.text: A Physical Parser MUST read a field that declares bddo:terminator by these rules:

req-pm-terminators-2.text: The terminator is the byte sequence given by bddo:terminator; an empty terminator is a description error.

req-pm-terminators-3.text: The search starts at the cursor and finds the first occurrence of the sequence that lies entirely within the search bound. For a bddo:string whose bddo:encoding has a multi-byte code unit (bddo:utf16le, bddo:utf16be), only occurrences that start at an offset from the search start that is a multiple of the code-unit size (2) count, so a terminator can never match across two code units. For every other encoding and for bytes the search is byte-aligned.

req-pm-terminators-4.text: The value is the bytes from the search start up to, and excluding, the terminator. The terminator is consumed: it is part of the field's byte extent but not of its value.

req-pm-terminators-5.text: With a declared region, the cursor then moves to the end of the region (the bytes after the terminator are padding); without one, the cursor moves to just after the terminator.

req-pm-terminators-6.text: If no occurrence lies within the search bound, raise a bounds error.

req-pm-text-numbers-1.text: The scan is byte-wise, so the field's encoding MUST be UTF-8, US-ASCII or ISO-8859-1; any other is a validation error.

req-pm-text-numbers-2.text: A Physical Parser MUST read these self-describing values as follows:

req-pm-text-numbers-3.text: Text numbers. A field of bddo:asciiInteger or bddo:asciiDecimal (or any type with an integer or float base type and no bit width) is read from its extent () and decoded per its bddo:encoding. Surrounding whitespace and NUL bytes and a leading + are removed. An integer is then read in radix bddo:numericBase (8, 10 or 16; default 10); a decimal accepts a sign, a decimal point, and an exponent introduced by E, e, D or d, and the spelling nan in any case with an optional sign. Anything else, including an infinite value, is a validation error: the value is never kept as a string.

req-pm-text-numbers-4.text: Varints. bddo:varuint is LEB128: seven value bits per byte, least-significant group first, the high bit set on every byte but the last. bddo:varint is a LEB128 value carrying a zigzag-encoded signed integer. bddo:sqliteVarint is one to nine big-endian bytes, the high bit of each of the first eight a continuation flag and the ninth contributing all eight bits. A varint that runs past its bound, or that exceeds the 64-bit range, is a bounds error.

req-pm-tree-documents-1.text: An XML parser MUST NOT fetch external entities or DTDs, and entity expansion counts toward the resource limits; a processor MAY decline to process a document type declaration at all, and a reference to an entity that only a declaration would define is then a validation error (the reference implementation processes no DTD, so the billion-laughs and external-entity attacks both end there).

req-pm-tree-documents-2.text: A reference to an external entity MUST be reported as a validation error whether or not the processor reads the declaration, since the entity's text is never fetched.

req-pm-typed-cells-1.text: A value that does not parse as the declared number is a validation error; it MUST NOT be kept as a string, because an expression reading a declared number cannot tell such a string from a real one.

req-hel-coercion-1.text: Arithmetic / bitwise operands MUST be numeric.

req-hel-coercion-2.text: Integer comparisons MUST be exact; mixed comparisons compare the exact represented numeric values without first rounding the Integer to Float.

req-hel-conformance-2.text: Parse all valid expressions per the ABNF grammar, and reject as a syntax error every string it does not generate, including out-of-range literals and unknown escapes.

req-hel-conformance-3.text: A processor that does not parse multi-part assets MAY leave asset and partExtension unimplemented, but MUST then raise a runtime error on an expression that uses them rather than resolving them to Null.

req-hel-conformance-4.text: Implement all operators and every core function with the specified precedence, the numeric semantics, and the value-type and coercion rules; and implement each extension group it claims in full.

req-hel-conformance-5.text: Reject, at load time, a description that calls a function of an extension group it does not implement, with an unsupported-feature error.

req-hel-conformance-6.text: Yield a Boolean in a boolean context, an Integer in a numeric context and a String in a string context, as the name-binding table gives for each property (e.g. a hexplain:valueExpression whose hexplain:valueDatatype is xsd:string yields a String); any other result is an error, and a Float is never an Integer, even one whose value is integral: a size expression that yields 2.0 is an error, not a size of 2.

req-hel-conformance-7.text: Report a runtime error (rather than silently continue) on type errors, integer overflow, shift counts out of range, out-of-range unsigned values, division/modulo by zero, out-of-range subscripts, undefined names and forward references.

req-hel-conformance-8.text: Accept, by default, expressions whose expression tree is at least 512 levels deep and at least 64 KiB long, when they are parsed and when they are evaluated; let the user configure both limits; and report an expression beyond its configured nesting or length limit, a quantifier that exceeds its evaluation budget, and a deadline or cancellation as the Processing Model's ResourceLimit error, not as a syntax or runtime error: it is fatal in every mode, including a lenient one that records other errors and continues.

req-hel-conformance-9.text: Produce, for every row of hel-vectors.tsv whose functions it implements, the value the row gives, or an error whose diagnostic contains the row's text.

req-hel-conformance-10.text: An evaluator MUST count depth this way, so that a long flat sum or conjunction, which descriptions generate, is accepted whatever its length allows.

req-hel-core-functions-1.text: A conforming evaluator MUST implement every core function.

req-hel-core-functions-2.text: Every argument MUST already be a String (or Bytes): there is no implicit conversion, so a number must be rendered deliberately rather than picking up whatever spelling the engine happens to use for it.

req-hel-core-functions-3.text: Integer or Float: the numeric value of string, whose lexical form MUST match NumericText below exactly.

req-hel-core-functions-4.text: The accessor MUST be exactly asset.<Part>, naming a part (e.g. partExtension(asset.Raster)); it is a runtime error otherwise, when the part is missing or more than one file was matched to it, and — like asset itself — when the description is not being parsed as part of an asset.

req-hel-ext-quantifiers-1.text: The first argument MUST be an array node.

req-hel-ext-quantifiers-2.text: Each evaluation MUST yield a Boolean, else it is an error.

req-hel-ext-temporal-1.text: The text MUST supply a full date and time.

req-hel-ext-temporal-2.text: Resolution is strict: every field MUST be in range for the date it names, so 30 February, day 00, month 13 or hour 24 is not a valid date-time and is never rolled over into another date.

req-hel-ext-temporal-3.text: It is a parameter supplied to the run: an evaluator MUST take it from the run and MUST NOT read it from the wall clock, so that re-running the same evidence gives identical results.

req-hel-ext-text-2.text: Profiles SHOULD confine patterns to the constructs common to the major regular-expression dialects — literal characters, ., bracket classes with ranges and negation, * + ? {m,n}, |, grouping with ( ), and the escapes \d \s \w — whose meaning is the same everywhere; the meaning of other constructs is implementation-defined.

req-hel-extension-groups-1.text: A processor that does not implement a group MUST reject a description whose expressions call a function of that group when the description is loaded, with an unsupported-feature error naming the function and the group's IRI; it MUST NOT defer the failure to the first evaluation, where it would depend on the data.

req-hel-formal-grammar-1.text: HEL and HDL string literals share one escape set: \\ (backslash), \' (apostrophe), \" (quotation mark), \n (U+000A), \t (U+0009), \r (U+000D), \0 (U+0000), \xHH (the code point U+0000–U+00FF given by exactly two hex digits) and \uHHHH (the UTF-16 code unit given by exactly four hex digits; a high surrogate MUST be followed by a \uHHHH low surrogate, the pair denoting one code point, and a lone surrogate is an error).

req-hel-formal-grammar-2.text: An IntegerLiteral or HexLiteral denotes a non-negative Integer and MUST NOT exceed 263−1 (9223372036854775807, 0x7FFFFFFFFFFFFFFF); a larger literal is a syntax error, not a wrap-around.

req-hel-key-resolution-1.text: Within one struct, field local names MUST be unique.

req-hel-key-resolution-2.text: A key MUST name a field declared by the bddo:Struct of the node it is applied to, or be the keyword parent; this is checked at every step of a path, not only the first, and inside the predicate of all/any a bare name is checked against the element's struct.

req-hel-key-resolution-3.text: A name that is also a reserved word (instance parent root self stream asset and or not true false) cannot be written as a bare name or a key, so a field that expressions need to reference MUST NOT have such a local name.

req-hel-key-resolution-4.text: The index expression MUST evaluate to a non-negative Integer strictly less than the array's length (elements are 0-based); otherwise a range error is raised.

req-hel-key-resolution-5.text: A processor MUST reject a description in which two fields of one struct share a local name, with a Description error when the description is loaded: an expression could not tell which of them a name reads.

req-hel-name-binding-1.text: The table below is normative and complete: these are the HEL-bearing properties, and for each, what the roots instance, parent, root and self are bound to and what type the result MUST have.

req-hel-name-binding-2.text: New descriptions MUST NOT use it; a processor SHOULD warn when it loads a description that does; an HDL compiler never emits it.

req-hel-numeric-semantics-1.text: Integer-only +, -, *, / and unary - are exact within [−263, 263−1]; a result outside that range MUST raise an error, never wrap.

req-hel-numeric-semantics-2.text: Division and modulo by zero MUST raise an error, for Float operands as well as Integer ones: 1.0 / 0.0 is an error, not Infinity.

req-hel-numeric-semantics-3.text: The shift count MUST be an Integer in [0, 63]; a count outside that range MUST raise an error (it is not reduced modulo 64). >> is an arithmetic (sign-propagating) right shift.

req-hel-numeric-semantics-4.text: x << n MUST raise an error when x × 2n is outside the signed 64-bit range, so 1 << 63 is an error.

req-hel-numeric-semantics-5.text: A parsed unsigned integer above 263−1 (from a uint64 field) keeps its exact value for comparisons and for Float arithmetic, but its use in Integer arithmetic, bitwise operations, shifts or indexes MUST raise an out-of-range error.

req-hel-numeric-semantics-6.text: Indexes MUST be non-negative Integers within the addressed collection; a Float, negative or out-of-range index MUST raise an error.

req-hel-operator-precedence-1.text: A guard MUST therefore be written with the ternary rather than with and: count(Items) > 0 ? Items[0] == 1 : false, not count(Items) > 0 and Items[0] == 1.

req-hel-operator-precedence-2.text: The ternary evaluates its condition (which must yield a Boolean) and then only the selected branch; both branches SHOULD have compatible types, and the result takes the type of the selected branch.

req-hel-operator-precedence-3.text: The operands of and, or and not MUST be Booleans, and both operands of and and or are type-checked: false and 1 is an error even though false decides the result.

req-hel-operator-precedence-4.text: The logical and and or operators MUST evaluate BOTH operands: they do not short-circuit, so an expression whose right operand raises — a division by zero, an out-of-range subscript — raises even when the left operand already decides the result.

req-hel-reserved-roots-1.text: The key after the part name MUST name a field of that part's root struct.

req-hel-tonumber-1.text: The String argument MUST match this grammar in its entirety:

req-hel-undefined-names-1.text: Three cases are distinguished, and a conforming evaluator MUST keep them apart:

req-hel-undefined-names-2.text: A key that names no field declared by the addressed struct (a typo, or a field of some other struct), or self where the property defines no value under test, MUST raise an undefined-name error.

req-hel-undefined-names-3.text: It MUST NOT evaluate to Null: a misspelt name that read as Null would silently turn a presence condition false or a comparison false.

req-hel-undefined-names-4.text: A key that names a declared field which has not yet been reached at the moment of evaluation (it comes later in field order, or belongs to a struct instance still being parsed further on) MUST raise a forward-reference error.

req-hel-undefined-names-5.text: Absent optional field. A declared field that has been reached but is not present in this instance (its bddo:isPresentIf was false) reads as Null. This is the only way a field reference yields Null.

req-hel-versioning-1.text: A later 1.x version MAY add functions and extension groups, but MUST NOT change the value or the error an expression that is valid under HEL 1.0 produces.

req-hel-versioning-2.text: The function library is divided into a core set, which every conforming evaluator MUST implement, and named extension groups, which an evaluator MAY implement.

req-hdl-clauses-1.text: An integer @fixed on a numeric field is emitted typed with the field's XSD type (@fixed 9994 on an i32 becomes "9994"^^xsd:int) and is compared by value; a hex @fixed stays xsd:hexBinary and, on a numeric field, MUST have exactly the field's width in bytes (Processing Model, Fixed value).

req-hdl-clauses-2.text: A field MUST NOT carry two clauses of one kind, and a compiler MUST report an ERROR for a second size (two […]), count (two repeat), offset (two @at), fixed value (two @fixed), byte order (two @endian) or type selection (two of switch and dispatch), rather than emit both values of a property the Processing Model reads once.

req-hdl-clauses-3.text: It MUST also report an ERROR for a derive field with a repeat clause (a derived field reads no bytes, so it has no elements), for @pipeline together with @encoded-with on one field, and for two declarations of one struct, header, table or document name in a document.

req-hdl-clauses-4.text: A compiler MUST report an ERROR for a literal outside the range of its position — a field size or struct @size below 1 (bytes[0], bytes[-3]), a repeat count or offset below 0 (repeat -2, @at -2), a stride below 1 (stride 0) — and for a FLOAT literal in any of these positions (bytes[2.0], repeat 1.5, @at 1e0): they take integers, and an integral float is not one.

req-hdl-clauses-5.text: The literal positions differ in what they accept, and a compiler MUST hold each to its own set. @prop takes an IRIREF, a CURIE, or an INT, HEX, STRING, true or false literal, never a bare NAME (write the string "x" or the CURIE ex:x).

req-hdl-compilation-model-1.text: Errors at any stage are reported as diagnostics with a source location; a conforming compiler MUST NOT raise an uncaught exception to its caller on malformed input, and MUST report at least one ERROR diagnostic for input it cannot faithfully compile.

req-hdl-conformance-section-2.text: Accept both the text and YAML surfaces and parse each into the same abstract model, such that a text document and its YAML mirror compile to isomorphic RDF graphs — except for the text-only constructs module, import, dispatch/extend dispatch and @seek, which the YAML surface rejects with a diagnostic.

req-hdl-conformance-section-3.text: Accept every text-surface document generated by the grammar (subject to the static rules stated alongside it) and report an ERROR diagnostic for any text-surface input it does not generate.

req-hdl-conformance-section-4.text: Mint IRIs per §IRI Minting and bind prefixes per §Prefixes; a CURIE whose prefix is not bound MUST yield an ERROR diagnostic, never a warning and never a silently emitted IRI.

req-hdl-conformance-section-5.text: Apply the field-form-vs-expression-form rule and resolve expression identifiers per §Expressions and the HEL name-binding rules, emitting canonical HEL validated against [[?hel]]; a bare reference to an undeclared name MUST yield an ERROR diagnostic, and so MUST every other static error §Expressions lists, a forward reference included, wherever it is statically determinable (§Expressions): the compiler knows the declaration order of every struct it compiles, so every bare-name forward reference, and every root.

req-hdl-conformance-section-6.text: Emit BDDO/Core/DLV/hx-bundle triples whose meaning matches the mappings in this document, such that the output satisfies the SHACL shapes of the targeted vocabularies for any well-formed input.

req-hdl-conformance-section-7.text: Report malformed input as source-located diagnostics and never raise an uncaught exception to its caller; input that cannot be faithfully compiled MUST yield at least one ERROR diagnostic.

req-hdl-conformance-section-8.text: Preserve raw-turtle bodies verbatim in the output graph.

req-hdl-conformance-section-9.text: Report an ERROR for a field name or alias that is not an ASCII HEL identifier or is reserved (asset included; §Lexical Structure), and for every layout name that does not name a sibling (§Expressions).

req-hdl-conformance-section-10.text: By default, confine import resolution to an import root (the root document's directory unless the caller names another) and reject, with an ERROR, any import whose real path lies outside it (Import resolution). A compiler MAY offer an explicit unrestricted mode for trusted callers.

req-hdl-conformance-section-11.text: Report an ERROR diagnostic for a language version declaration naming a version it does not implement.

req-hdl-expressions-1.text: A conforming compiler MUST validate every synthesized expression against the HEL grammar and MUST report an ERROR diagnostic, at compile time, for: a bare identifier that does not resolve to a declared field; a forward reference, including a field's reference to itself outside @valid; self outside repeat until, @valid and a quantifier predicate; a stream.

req-hdl-expressions-2.text: The names in a layout — a dimension's size and chunk, cell-bits from, chunks offsets/lengths, a stride expression, and the guards of cell switch and order switch — are sibling references like any other: each MUST name a field of the containing struct, and an unknown one is an ERROR.

req-hdl-expressions-3.text: A root.k path whose k is not a field of the root struct is an undeclared name, except when some struct of the document declares @root-key: k may then be a key only the data names (Processing Model, Root key), and a compiler MUST then accept root.k for any identifier k.

req-hdl-expressions-4.text: A compiler MUST resolve the names of a repeat until condition as follows.

req-hdl-expressions-5.text: A compiler MUST report an ERROR for a key step applied to a field that holds a scalar (n.foo), or to a repeated field without a subscript (es.size; the number of elements is len(es)): neither has fields.

req-hdl-form-rule-1.text: For any size, offset, or count clause: when the expression is exactly one sibling field name, a conforming compiler MUST emit the specific …FromField object property; otherwise it MUST emit the …FromExpression datatype property carrying the synthesized HEL string.

req-hdl-form-rule-2.text: A compiler MUST emit every integer it writes as an xsd:integer literal (Turtle's bare integer), except where this document names another datatype: a size, repeat count, offset, alignment, radix, bit length, skip count, dimension size, stride, chunk extent, cell width, part count, enumeration raw value, dispatch key, pipeline parameter or @prop value is an xsd:integer, never an xsd:long or xsd:int, whatever range the targeted property declares; an integer @fixed on a numeric field takes the field's XSD type (Fixed values).

req-hdl-grammar-1.text: It defines the complete text surface of HDL: a conforming compiler MUST accept every document the grammar generates (subject to the static rules below and elsewhere in this document) and MUST report an ERROR diagnostic for any document it does not generate.

req-hdl-grammar-document-1.text: A format document MUST declare at least one struct or container unless it declares a bundle or asset; the struct marked @root, else the first struct, is the root.

req-hdl-grammar-expressions-1.text: Every Expr, Guard and CoverExpr denotes a HEL expression: after the rewriting of §Expressions, its text MUST match the Expression production of the HEL grammar.

req-hdl-grammar-expressions-2.text: Backtick (` … `): the text is raw HEL, emitted verbatim with no rewriting at all, so it MUST already be valid HEL (single-quoted strings, no 0b literals, explicit instance.

req-hdl-grammar-expressions-3.text: Backticks are all or nothing: a BACKTICK_EXPR MUST be the whole Expr or Guard; one inside a longer run is an ERROR.

req-hdl-grammar-fields-1.text: A PipelineStep parameter value MUST be an integer literal (§Semantic Mapping).

req-hdl-grammar-keywords-1.text: instance parent root self stream asset and or not true false — HEL reads them as roots, operators or literals, so a compiler MUST reject a field or alias so named.

req-hdl-grammar-layout-1.text: Every NAME in a layout (sizes, chunk extents, cell-bits from, offsets, lengths, stride expressions, guards) is a sibling reference and MUST name a field of the containing struct.

req-hdl-grammar-lexical-1.text: A NAME used as a field name or alias MUST additionally be a HEL identifier (§Lexical Structure).

req-hdl-layout-1.text: This example reads values from another part of a multi-file asset (asset.Header.…) and the grid part's own extension (partExtension(asset.Grid); a part is named by the struct its part spec is described-by), so it can only be processed by a processor in the Bundle Processor conformance class (Processing Model §Conformance classes); a Physical Parser handed the raster part alone MUST fail the asset references with an error rather than read them as Null.

req-hdl-lexical-1.text: Although the lexer folds - and ., a field's name and its as alias MUST be HEL identifiers — an ASCII letter or _ followed by ASCII letters, digits and _, and not one of instance parent root self stream asset and or not true false — because expressions reach a field by that name (asset is HEL's multi-part root, so a field so named could never be read).

req-hdl-lexical-2.text: A compiler MUST report an ERROR for a hyphenated, dotted or reserved field name (the reference compiler suggests byte_order for byte-order).

req-hdl-lexical-3.text: Digits are ASCII only: a compiler MUST report a lexical ERROR for a non-ASCII digit (the Arabic-Indic ٣, the fullwidth １) outside a string, comment or raw-turtle block, never read it as a digit.

req-hdl-modules-1.text: An import path is resolved relative to the directory of the file that contains it, and MUST resolve within an import root.

req-hdl-modules-2.text: escape, or a symbolic link pointing out of the tree, since links are resolved to their real path before the check — MUST be rejected with an ERROR diagnostic on the import line; the root is inherited by every nested import, so an imported module cannot widen it.

req-hdl-prefixes-1.text: In particular, aspect and register prefixes (araster, acolor, ageom, menc, and the part-role register's own conventional prefix rpr, which is bound to the same namespace as role) are not predeclared: a description that uses one MUST bind it with use.

req-hdl-prefixes-2.text: A CURIE whose prefix is none of the above — not predeclared, not bound by use, and not an import alias — is an error: a conforming compiler MUST report an ERROR diagnostic for it wherever it occurs (a means, @datatype, @encoded-with, @pipeline step, @object, @unit, @prop, enum symbol, register, part role, carries, or type position), and MUST NOT emit the unexpanded CURIE as an IRI.

req-hdl-types-1.text: A compiler MUST report an ERROR for a bracket size after a fixed-width numeric type (u8 … f64be) or a variable-length integer type: the Processing Model ignores a size on a fixed-width field, so u32[4] could only mislead its reader into expecting four bytes of something else, or four elements.

req-hdl-versioning-1.text: A compiler that does not recognise the declaration, or that recognises it but does not implement the version named, MUST report an ERROR diagnostic (unsupported language version) and MUST NOT compile the document under the rules of a different version.

req-hdl-yaml-1.text: A conforming YAML loader MUST restrict implicit boolean resolution to true/false; the YAML 1.1 words on/off/yes/no are strings (so a struct field or switch key named on is not silently coerced).

req-hdl-yaml-2.text: A conforming YAML loader MUST report an ERROR for a mapping that repeats a key (YAML leaves the outcome to the loader, and last-wins would drop a field or a clause silently) and for a null entry in a sequence (a stray - in a field list), rather than skip it.

req-ce-conf-conformance-1.text: A processor that evaluates profiles is a Conformance Evaluator, and MUST follow Processing Model §Conformance Evaluation.

req-ce-conf-conformance-2.text: A constraint whose conf:scope is a bddo:Struct MUST be evaluated once per parsed instance, with instance and self bound to it; one whose scope is a bddo:Field MUST be evaluated once per parsed value of the field, with instance bound to the containing struct and self to the value.

req-ce-conf-conformance-3.text: A false assertion MUST yield exactly one conf:Violation finding at the constraint's conf:severity, citing every requirement the constraint cites; any other result, or an evaluation failure, MUST yield one conf:RuleError finding.

req-ce-conf-conformance-4.text: A finding MUST NOT cite a requirement its constraint does not cite.

req-ce-conf-conformance-5.text: A parse error MUST be reported as a conf:Parse finding with its conf:errorCategory, attributed to the requirement of the profile's conf:ParseAttribution for that category, or to no requirement when none names it.

req-ce-conf-conformance-6.text: conf:message placeholders MUST be interpolated as that property defines: {field} is the focus node's path, and {value} the evaluated value when it is unambiguous, left as written otherwise.

req-ce-conf-conformance-7.text: Version scoping MUST use only a version the caller supplies, compared with req:appliesToVersion by exact string equality.

req-ce-conf-conformance-8.text: Without one, every requirement MUST be evaluated and the report MUST say that version scoping was not applied.

req-ce-conf-conformance-9.text: A run stopped by a resource limit MUST either fail with a ResourceLimit error or be reported as truncated; requirements it did not reach MUST receive conf:NotReached.

req-ce-conf-conformance-10.text: Every requirement of the profile MUST receive exactly one outcome, with the precedence conf:NotApplicable > conf:Errored > conf:Evaluated > conf:NotReached > conf:NotExercised; a requirement no constraint cites is conf:NotExercised.

req-ce-req-conformance-1.text: It MUST carry exactly one non-empty req:requirementId, req:fromStandard and req:statement, and exactly one req:discrepancyType.

req-ce-req-conformance-2.text: Within one graph, two distinct requirements MUST NOT carry the same (req:fromStandard, req:requirementId) pair after surrounding whitespace is removed from both values and req:fromStandard is compared ignoring case; req:RequirementIdentityShape enforces it.

req-ce-req-conformance-3.text: req:appliesToVersion values are compared by exact string equality with the input's format version, which the caller of a conformance run supplies; an evaluator MUST NOT infer it (Processing Model §Conformance Evaluation).

req-ce-req-conformance-4.text: req:discrepancyType classifies a defect and MUST NOT be used to set a finding's severity; severity is the citing constraint's conf:severity.
